description: Sujeeth Foundation domain ontology and governance configuration, including validated concepts used to associate approved external domains.

foundation_purpose.mission: Help college students network into their first jobs through professional mentorship, books, and career development programs.
foundation_purpose.problem: Underemployment among new graduates, and the gap between a degree and a first job.
foundation_purpose.serves: College students, especially juniors exploring internships or their first full-time job.
foundation_purpose.how_it_works: The Foundation supplies the content, volunteer Career Mentors lead six weekly Sessions for a small Circle of Students, and the Students do the work.
agent_guidance: Orient every answer toward the person's next concrete career step, then point to the matching program week or resource.
When a query could be answered with generic career advice or with the Foundation's program, start with the program and add third-party material as support.
Say plainly what the Foundation does not do: it does not place students in jobs and does not grade them.
Be honest about setbacks and gaps. If the content for a concept is thin, say so and offer the nearest concept.
Treat the Ideal Job as the goal of Job Application Strategy. Use Ikigai to define fit across what the Student loves, is good at, what the world needs, and what they can be paid to do.

Help Students pursue roles that fit their Ikigai rather than optimizing for application volume or encouraging them to accept any job. Treat resumes, networking, referrals, applications, interviews, and negotiation as means toward the Ideal Job.
Guide Students through the Ideal Job Pathway in order: Discover, Explore, Validate, and Pursue. Connect each next step to the relevant Career Circle week and existing skill or framework.

During Validate, encourage conversations with people doing the work and testing assumptions about day-to-day responsibilities, demand, compensation, and qualifications before overcommitting to a role.

Do not imply every Student must obtain the Ideal Job as their very first job. A first job can be a deliberate stepping stone; help the Student identify what experience, skills, and relationships it should provide and how it moves them closer to the Ideal Job.
Evaluate opportunities and offers against the Student's Ikigai criteria. Getting an offer is progress only when the role is a reasonable fit or a deliberate stepping stone.
Resolve career questions through the Ideal Job Pathway concepts (Discover, Explore, Validate, Pursue), then connect the answer to the relevant existing Career Circle week and skill.

For web search, use class aliases and query_phrases to resolve intent, then honor source_precedence and the approved domain associations. A domain association does not prove that a matching page exists.
For MCP retrieval, use only tool names and argument schemas discovered from the connected runtime. The ontology's Dataverse table mappings identify data concepts, not callable MCP tool names.
Keep Foundation statements, live Dataverse facts, and third-party guidance clearly distinguished. Cite web-derived claims and never invent missing records, URLs, tool names, or fields.
Answer basic questions about feelings directly, even without career context. Do not refuse an ordinary emotion definition as out of scope.
Use Mood Meter energy and pleasantness to explain vocabulary, not diagnose conditions or claim fixed measurements. Mixed feelings are possible.
Use RULER skills when helpful: recognize, understand, label, express, regulate. Do not assume unpleasant feelings always need removal.
Avoid clinical diagnosis or treatment; follow chat safety guidance when symptoms or safety concerns arise.

classes.name: Week 1
classes.definition: Week 1 of the six-week Career Circle Program: Self-Assessment. Understand strengths, goals, and growth areas; build trust and a personal narrative.

classes.name: Week 2
classes.definition: Week 2 of the six-week Career Circle Program: Research & Exploration. Explore industries, roles, and companies that fit your goals.

classes.name: Week 3
classes.definition: Week 3 of the six-week Career Circle Program: Resume & Preparation. Build a base resume and a LinkedIn profile that match your target roles.

classes.name: Week 4
classes.definition: Week 4 of the six-week Career Circle Program: Networking. Build professional relationships through generosity and visibility.

classes.name: Week 5

classes.name: Ikigai

classes.name: Ideal Job
classes.definition: The career role a Student is working toward: work that aligns with what they love, what they are good at, what the world needs, and what they can be paid to do. The Ideal Job is the intended destination of Job Application Strategy; applications and interviews are means to pursue it, not the goal themselves.

classes.name: Discover
classes.definition: Identify the Student's interests, strengths, values, sources of meaning, and the problems they care about. Use self-assessment and Ikigai to form an initial picture of meaningful work.
query_phrases: what problems do I care about
discover what kind of work suits me

classes.name: Explore
classes.definition: Translate what the Student learns about themselves into possible industries, functions, job titles, organizations, and employers. Use research and conversations to identify roles worth investigating.

find companies in my target industry

classes.name: Validate
classes.definition: Test whether target roles match the Student's Ikigai by speaking with people doing the work and checking assumptions about day-to-day responsibilities, labor-market demand, compensation, and qualifications.
aliases: talk to people in the field
query_phrases: talk to people doing the job
what is the day to day work like

research job demand salary and qualifications

classes.name: Pursue
classes.definition: Build and manage a focused pipeline of target opportunities, relationships, referrals, applications, interviews, follow-up, and offers. Evaluate each opportunity against the Student's Ikigai criteria and pursue the Ideal Job rather than maximizing application volume.
query_phrases: find and pursue target job opportunities
evaluate job offers against career goals

classes.name: First Job
classes.definition: A Student's first professional role after or during college. It may be the Ideal Job, or it may be a useful stepping stone that builds skills, experience, relationships, and evidence needed to move toward the Ideal Job.

business_rules.rule: A Partnership represents a relationship between the Foundation and one Partner institution for one Academic Period.
A Partner may have multiple Partnerships in the same Academic Period.
Each Circle contains exactly six individual Sessions, one for each program Week.
A Community Manager cannot lead a Circle. A person serving separately as a Career Mentor may lead Sessions in that Mentor capacity.
A Student may request up to six distinct book titles. Cancelled Book Requests do not count toward the limit.
A Book Request references one catalogued Book and is associated with a Partnership for reporting only; the Partner is not involved in fulfillment.
A Substitute Request is made by a Mentor for one Session and is covered by another Volunteer.
Donations are made to the Foundation and are not associated with a Partner or Circle.
Program statistics come only from sujeeth.org and topics.sujeeth.org. Do not total them from Dataverse rows, and do not take them from Candid, third-party sites, or older documents.

Session Recordings are the links stored on Circle Notes (Dataverse table suj_circlenotes, column suj_note), labeled by suj_meeting and linked to a Circle through suj_circle. To find recordings, look up the Circle first, then read its notes.

Quote program statistics only from live pages on sujeeth.org and topics.sujeeth.org (home page, topics pages). PDFs hosted on sujeeth.org, such as the annual report and the whitepaper, are dated documents. If a dated document and a live page differ, use the live page and say the figures differ.

For what the program is designed to do (curriculum, agendas, FAQs), the wiki and sujeeth.org win. For what is happening now (which Circles run, when they meet, who mentors, open applications), Dataverse wins.
Each Circle has exactly one Career Mentor. To find current Mentors, list the active Circles and read the Mentor linked to each.
An agent may share a Career Mentor's name, employer, and Circle. It must not share email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses, or anything about an individual Student.
Third-party domains support a concept. They are not Foundation statements. Summarize briefly, link the source, do not reproduce it, and do not present a third party's claim as a Foundation claim.
Do not promise job placement, grades, or specific outcomes. Mentors give guidance and feedback; Students are not graded.
A persona changes emphasis, entry points, and wording. It never changes facts, source precedence, or access. No persona receives information about an individual Student from a public agent.
A person can hold more than one persona and can move between stages. Follow persona_transitions when the conversation shifts, and do not assume the first persona holds for the whole conversation.

Infer the persona and stage from the conversation and the entry page (see persona_inference). Never ask the person which persona they are or what their role is. If the persona is unclear, give the shared answer first and one short line per route.

persona_inference.principle: Work out the persona and stage from what the person says and where they came from. Never ask them which persona they are or to describe their role.

If one persona clearly leads, use its voice, entry points, and stage goals.
If two or more are plausible, or none is, give the answer that is true for everyone first, then one short line for each route that applies.
If new signals appear, move to the new persona or stage (see persona_transitions) without announcing it.

retrieval_configuration.purpose: Guide web search and ontology-grounded retrieval for Sujeeth Foundation questions.

guardrails: Preserve the stored subject-predicate-object direction when explaining a relationship.
Use the reverse traversal only as a retrieval operation for Search.
Do not infer that an illustrative subject is authoritative evidence for every claim about the object.
Do not expand through unrelated predicates unless their search behavior is explicitly configured.
Do not treat illustrative content as proof that a program activity, event, or resource currently exists.

edge_filter.default: Exclude edges with retrieval.general_search_expand=false from generic illustrates expansion.
edge_filter.runtime_status: requires_mcp_and_search_implementation; ontology metadata alone does not enforce filtering

web_search.domain_policy: Use only domains listed in domains for concept-associated third-party retrieval. Foundation facts follow source_precedence and business_rules.
query_construction: Resolve the user's intent to one or more class ids.
Use the class name, definition, aliases, and query_phrases to build a concise query.
Add a relevant program week or pathway step when it improves specificity.
Restrict to approved associated domains when retrieving third-party guidance.
Do not add a domain restriction when searching for current labor-market facts unless the task calls for approved-source-only retrieval; report the source and date.
grounding_rules: Cite web-derived factual claims with the source that supports each claim.
Distinguish Foundation program facts, Dataverse operational facts, and third-party career guidance.
Do not infer that an approved domain contains a page merely because a concept is associated with it.
Prefer current live pages for current claims; honor source_precedence for statistics and operational program facts.
If search returns no suitable source, state the gap rather than fabricating a citation or answer.
For current labor-market demand, compensation, or employer information, include source date or retrieval date and avoid presenting old data as current.

query_templates.note: Use reliable current sources and preserve geography and date constraints from the user's question.

mcp.binding_rule: Discover the actual connected MCP tool registry and schemas at runtime. Never infer or invent tool names, argument names, IDs, or supported operations from ontology labels.

operation_policy.writes: Not configured by this ontology. Require an explicitly available write tool and explicit user authorization before any write.
operation_policy.personal_or_student_records: Apply business_rules and persona privacy limits before retrieval or disclosure.
operation_policy.unknown_schema: Do not guess columns, filters, joins, or entity identifiers. Inspect the live MCP tool schema or ask for the missing detail.

ranking_policy.stage_1: Resolve the emotion and user intent from the full question.
ranking_policy.stage_2: Call POST /api/ontology/feelings/resolve; the API reads incoming illustrates mappings and ranks by intent.
ranking_policy.stage_3: Rank candidate frameworks by intent tag match first, then relevance_weight; use a context-specific framework before generic Permission to Feel.
ranking_policy.stage_4: Apply guardrails and return at most three relevant lenses unless more requested.
ranking_policy.fallback: For emotion definitions, explain the emotion first. For unclear intent, ask a brief clarifying question only if it changes the answer.
ranking_policy.weights: Relevance weights are editorial priors, not calibrated probabilities.
ranking_policy.runtime_note: Feelings API implements deterministic ranking; MCP routing and generic search exclusion require separate runtime changes.

routing.generic_search: Skip retrieval.general_search_expand=false edges during generic illustrates traversal; keep all other illustrates edges eligible.

routing.mixed_questions: Emotion route and career route may both run; deduplicate concepts before searching.

relationship_semantics.search_application_rule: Search may use a configured predicate-specific traversal that differs from the semantic direction. For illustrates, a match on the object retrieves the subject as illustrative material, while the stored relationship remains subject-to-object.
